description: How the cloud customer roles relate to each other: leaders chartering platform teams, platform operators paving roads and showing back cost, regulated owners gating workloads, and the marketplace flows where startups sell to enterprises against committed spend.

relationTypes.name: Commercial
relationTypes.description: Chartering teams and buying through the cloud marketplace

relationTypes.name: Operational
relationTypes.description: Paved roads, compliance gates, and workload delivery

relations.name: Charters the platform and FinOps organization
relations.description: Funds and mandates the platform, SRE, and FinOps function as part of the cloud operating model, setting the reliability, security, and unit-economics targets it must hit.

relations.name: Commissions modernization workloads
relations.description: Assigns application teams the migration and modernization waves in the portfolio plan, from rehosting legacy estates to rebuilding on managed runtimes.

relations.name: Provides paved-road landing zones
relations.description: Operates landing zones, golden paths, and CI/CD guardrails so builders ship on managed runtimes and data services without re-solving security and networking per team.

relations.name: Shows back cloud costs to product teams
relations.description: Allocates cloud spend to workloads with showback and chargeback, so builder teams see the unit cost of their services and act on rightsizing recommendations.

relations.name: Surfaces workload needs and incidents
relations.description: Raises service requests, capacity forecasts, and reliability signals from running workloads that shape what the platform paves next.

relations.name: Gates workloads through compliance controls
relations.description: Approves builder workloads for production against policy-as-code controls, data-residency rules, and audit evidence required in the regulated estate.

relations.name: Feeds regulatory constraints into the roadmap
relations.description: Translates sector regulation, sovereignty requirements, and audit findings into constraints the transformation leader must bake into the modernization roadmap.

relations.name: Reports cloud value and spend efficiency
relations.description: Reports migration progress, reliability, and unit economics against committed-spend agreements, giving leadership the numbers behind the business case.

relations.name: Directs the founding build team
relations.description: Sets the startup's architecture on managed services and drives its builders to ship and scale the product without owning infrastructure.

relations.name: Sells cloud-native products via the marketplace
relations.description: Offers the startup's SaaS to enterprises through cloud-marketplace private offers, riding the enterprise's existing procurement and cloud agreements.

relations.name: Retires committed spend on marketplace purchases
relations.description: Pays for the startup's product through the cloud marketplace, drawing the purchase down against the enterprise's committed-spend agreement.
